nodes.label: RPO 5 min / RTO 60 min Targets
nodes.rationale: These are objectives, not claims; a release may advertise them only after the quarterly isolated restore and regional exercise record timestamps that meet both budgets.

nodes.label: Encrypted age Recovery Bundle
nodes.rationale: backup.sh uses pg_dump custom format, captures integrity invariants, validates the object manifest, hashes every component, packages only four allowlisted files, encrypts with a KMS-controlled age recipient before publishing, and writes owner-only permissions; restore.sh refuses a target URL equal to the source and rejects traversal, links, and checksum mismatches before pg_restore.

nodes.label: Fail-Closed Restore Integrity Verification
nodes.rationale: A restore is not usable until ingest sequences, per-session replay positions, artifact SHA-256 hashes, and persisted action resolutions match the encrypted backup; application traffic stays disabled until schema health, tenant RLS, OIDC, Temporal visibility, object reads, stream replay, and a signed action canary all pass.

nodes.label: Expand/Backfill/Read-Switch/Contract Migration Sequencing
nodes.rationale: Every destructive schema change is split across releases so old and new binaries coexist; contract happens only after old binaries are drained and rollback has expired, and any lock over 30 seconds or observed old/new incompatibility blocks release.
